note: The manager's episode scenarios (NE-14j), recorded from the real PlayerQueueManager over the shared fakes: interruptions (and the INTERRUPTION_REWIND_SEC step back), routes, corner case #19's single audible start, cold launch, superseded loads, the double skip, pause silence, and position events. A step is a command, a deck event (DeckEvent), a session notification or a lifecycle moment; the op log is what the engine must command. Queue strategies stay in the page (plan §3 A-1): these scenarios hand the manager its queue. Port card NE-14s.

covers: queue-manager::play loads then starts, in that order
cases.note: The load carries the offset, the listener's rate is applied, then play: nothing audible before the asset is positioned.

covers: queue-manager::SINGLE_ITEM ends the session instead of chaining into another episode
cases.note: Nothing follows: the session ends, and nothing more is loaded (product principle 1).

covers: queue-manager::PICKED_FIRST advances to the next episode when one ends
queue-manager::a fast double-skip advances two items, not one
queue-manager::a fast double-skip loads only the final target
queue-manager::a concurrent double-skip lands on the final target and starts it once
cases.note: Corner case #19: two skips in flight at once load the final target (c) and start exactly one item. NE-14j recorded the JS landing on b (each effect was awaited, so the second skip's load(c) went out while the first skip was parked after its save, and the first skip's load(b) then superseded it). NE-14s fixed it JS first: the manager awaits only effects that are really asynchronous, so the first skip's save, pause and load(b) are one step, the second skip replaces the in-flight load, and c plays. That is also the native engine's order: one handle() turn per skip.

covers: queue-manager::a fast double-skip loads only the final target
cases.note: Corner case #19, single audible: with both skips' loads in flight, only the load that owns the deck starts audio; the other lands and plays nothing. Since NE-14s's JS fix (see the concurrent case above) b's load goes out first and c's replaces it, so c owns the deck: b landing is the silent one, and c's landing starts the one item.

covers: transport-reconcile::AUDIT: a load that lands after a newer one never claims the playhead
cases.note: A tap on a second episode while the first is still loading: the first load landing late plays nothing and stamps nothing (audit 2026-09-22).

covers: queue-manager::an interruption saves position and pauses
queue-manager::declined call resumes; answered call stays paused but ready
queue-manager::an OS should-resume steps back INTERRUPTION_REWIND_SEC on the item the element still holds
cases.note: INTERRUPTION_REWIND_SEC (plan §4.4, NE-14j): parked at 42.5 s, an OS should-resume reloads IN PLACE at 41 s (the backend's same-source seek), then rate, then play. Authored.

covers: queue-manager::the step back is the interruption's only: a listener's own resume lands where they paused
cases.note: Only an OS interruption steps back. The listener's own pause/play resumes at 42.5 s (@43), and a should-resume the manager declines (the listener had paused) arms nothing for the next load. Authored.

covers: queue-manager::an interruption's step back never crosses a segment's in-point (NE-14j)
cases.note: A segment [100, 210]: at 100.75 s the step back stops at the in-point (100), never in the stranger's episode before it; at 172.5 s it lands at 171 inside the slice, and the boundary is re-armed. Authored.

covers: queue-manager::a route disappearing pauses immediately
queue-manager::ROUND 2 review: a ROUTE LOSS is never resumed by a later call's should-resume (corner case #13)
queue-manager::ROUND 2 p-car-3: interruptionEnded(should-resume) resumes an OS interruption, never a listener's pause
transport-reconcile::ROUND 2 p-car-3: should-resume never resumes a pause the LISTENER made before the call
queue-manager::ROUND 2 review: a foreground reconcile of an external stop (#263, route gone while suspended) is not resumable
queue-manager::ROUND 2 review: the element's own unexplained pause (a call on an awake page) stays resumable
transport-reconcile::the backend's unexplained pause is wired to the reconcile
transport-reconcile::ROUND 2 p-car-3 (founder question 2): the call ends with should-resume, and 4a comes back on its own
queue-manager::cold launch prepares the asset AT the saved position, never seeking after play
queue-manager::cold launch without autoplay restores position without making noise
queue-manager::a resumed episode reloads at its saved position; a fresh one starts at zero
transport-reconcile::A COLD resume still reads the stored row — the fix above is not a mute
queue-manager::skipToPrevious restarts at zero, not at the playhead just saved
queue-manager::a skip saves the OUTGOING episode's position, never the incoming one's
queue-manager::every effect the reducer can emit has a handler
queue-manager::setRate snaps a junk or off-ladder value instead of handing it to the element
transport-reconcile::pause() is a postcondition, not a state transition: an audible element is silenced
cases.note: The postcondition of pause() is SILENCE (#689 report 3): paused already, the element audible again behind the machine, a second pause still reaches the element. The fixture half of record.mjs --mutate pause-silence.

Plan §5.5: every position write goes to cp_pos:<id>, and a position EVENT (the page's logEvent, the engine's pendingEvents row) goes out at most once per 60 media seconds per item — first save at 30 s (event), 75 s (no event: 45 s on), 95 s (event: 65 s on). Authored.
The once-a-minute mark is per item: skipping from a (saved at 40 s, its first event) to b and pausing b at 20 s emits b's own first event. Authored.

covers: transport-reconcile::REPRODUCTION: a stop the page never saw leaves the machine saying playing
transport-reconcile::reconciling corrects it, and ONE press then resumes where it stopped
transport-reconcile::the reconcile itself never starts audio
transport-reconcile::reconciling twice corrects once
transport-reconcile::an element that agrees with us is left alone
cases.note: #263, the founder's car: a deck that agrees is left alone; a stop nobody saw leaves the machine saying playing until it is asked; asking corrects it towards paused with no play, once however many triggers fire; and ONE press resumes where the deck stopped.

covers: transport-reconcile::a finished file is not an external stop
cases.note: Paused AND ended, with the end on its way: the reconcile leaves it to the end path, which then ends the session.

covers: transport-reconcile::playheadItemId names the item the element is holding, not the one we intend
transport-reconcile::a position is never written against an item the element is not holding
cases.note: The index moves before the load; the playhead only when a load lands. After a failed skip the deck still holds a, so a flush writes nothing for b and leaves a's row alone.

covers: transport-reconcile::REPORT 1: a route that DISAPPEARED pauses the transport and writes where it stopped
transport-reconcile::REPORT 2: an episode backgrounded while PAUSED remembers where it was paused
transport-reconcile::REPORT 1: the native BACKGROUND event flushes the position, with no visibilitychange
cases.note: A seek while paused saves the second being LEFT; leaving the foreground writes where the deck IS, paused or not.

covers: transport-reconcile::REPORT 4: pressing play resumes where the audio IS, not where the row says
cases.note: Re-entering the item the deck holds is a resume in place, from the scrub, not from the stale row.

covers: transport-reconcile::AUDIT: a superseded load that FAILS does not stop the load that replaced it
transport-reconcile::AUDIT: a cold start on a FINISHED episode begins at the top, not at the outro
cases.note: The stored second goes through the resume rule: inside the last 30 s is finished, and a finished episode starts at 0.

covers: transport-reconcile::AUDIT: play after an episode RAN OUT starts it again from the top
cases.note: The deck still holds the item at its last second, but it has ENDED, so a press is not a resume in place.

covers: transport-reconcile::ROUND 2 p-car-3: a STALE should-resume, a no-resume, and a resume the listener already did all change nothing
cases.note: The OS saying not to resume leaves it paused; once the listener has resumed it, a should-resume arriving after touches nothing. (The page's lag guard for a minute-old event is the WebView's: the engine hears the session live.)

covers: transport-reconcile::ROUND 2 player-3: a scrub made while paused survives Stop
cases.note: A seek while paused saves the second being LEFT and nothing writes while paused, so Stop (the page closing the bar, persist) writes where the deck IS before it stops.
